title: Ring editing: add, move and remove pinned points on an existing ring, re-tightening between pins
description:
Follow-on to CRAW-28 (user request 2026-09-06). CRAW-28 confirms a ring pinned at the one clicked point and renders that pin. This ticket makes rings editable afterwards: with the ring tool active, hovering an existing ring highlights it and its pins; clicking on the ring surface away from a pin adds a new pin there (the ring is re-tightened as a chain of fixed-endpoint FlipOut segments between consecutive pins, so it now passes through the new point); clicking an existing pin selects it, Delete/Backspace removes it (the two neighbouring segments merge and re-tighten; removing the last pin returns the ring to the unpinned geodesic, which slides to the neck); dragging a selected pin along the surface moves it with live re-tightening at preview rate. Pins are stored as the loop_through_points waypoints with pin=true, so every edit rewrites that ring's statement in the working .dsl in place (RingDslWriter gains replace-by-label) and the file reloads element-exact. Rings from ring_candidates become editable by pinning their first clicked point (which converts them into a loop_through_points statement). Undo for the last edit (one level) via Ctrl+Z. ui-state exposes pins per ring; the /input routes can drive every edit so run-scene can screenshot the sequence.

Redesign 2026-09-07: rings are splines through anchors (CRAW-28). Editing = drag an anchor (live re-trace of its two segments), click the ring to insert an anchor (CRAW-28 ships insertion; this ticket adds drag, delete, and one-level undo), select an anchor and Delete, optional corner anchors (C0 junction as in b/Surf) for deliberately sharp points, and an explicit 'tighten to neck' action on a selected ring that runs FlipOut with the ring's anchors held (FlipGeodesics.vertexIsPinned, loop_through_points pin=true) for the cases where the user wants the geodesic loop rather than the smooth one. Every edit rewrites the ring's spline_ring statement in place.

Redesign 2026-09-19 (user testing of the CRAW-28 tool in craw-rings): the one-click confirm plus scroll-to-tilt interaction is unwieldy and makes specific ring configurations hard to reach. This ticket replaces that interaction with a two-tier anchor model and a drafting state; it supersedes the drag/delete/undo design above, which becomes the editing half of the same model.

Two anchor classes on every ring. AUTHORED anchors are the points the user actually clicked: drawn in a distinct colour (cyan; yellow when selected), they are the only anchors the user can select, drag or delete, and they are what the saved statement records. SUPPORTING anchors are the ones SplineAnchorFit inserts to keep the traced spline within tolerance: drawn as today's smaller white discs, owned entirely by the fit, never selectable. The fit inserts and removes supporting anchors only between consecutive authored anchors and never moves an authored one; when an authored anchor moves or is added, only the segments whose control polygon changed are re-fitted, as insertAnchor already does. SurfaceSplineTracer gains a per-anchor authored flag; SplineAnchorFit gains the constraint.

Drafting state instead of one-click confirm. R starts the tool; hover previews the girdling spline as today. The first click on the surface turns the preview into a DRAFT ring and makes the clicked point its first authored anchor (the fit's evenly spaced anchors on that draft are supporting). While a draft exists hover no longer previews a new ring. Clicking the draft away from an anchor adds an authored anchor there; clicking an authored anchor selects it; Delete or Backspace removes the selected authored anchor (its neighbouring segments merge and are re-fitted; removing the last authored anchor discards the draft); dragging a selected authored anchor moves it along the surface with live re-trace at preview rate. Enter confirms the draft into the confirmed rings; Esc with a draft discards the draft; Esc with no draft leaves the tool, keeping every confirmed ring. Clicking a confirmed ring re-opens it as the draft (one draft at a time). Ctrl+Z undoes the last anchor edit on the draft, one level. Confirm and edits stay in memory; Ctrl+S saves as CRAW-28 shipped it.

Scroll tilt is removed from the wheel, which goes back to the orbit camera. With a second authored anchor available the plane estimate only needs to be roughly right; the anchors decide the ring. GirdlingPlane keeps its tilt fields for the automatic producers but the tool no longer exposes them.

Persistence: spline_ring writes the authored anchors only (points=), and reload re-runs the fit between them, which is deterministic, so the reloaded ring is element-exact against the live one (fingerprint equality, the existing SurfaceSplineTest reload case extended). A statement written by the CRAW-28 tool, whose anchors were all fitted, reloads with every anchor authored so nothing is lost. Rings from ring_candidates become editable when first clicked, converting to a spline_ring statement with the fit's anchors as authored.

Optional corner anchors (C0 junction as in b/Surf) and the explicit 'tighten to neck' action with anchors held (FlipGeodesics.vertexIsPinned, loop_through_points pin=true) stay in scope as before, keyed to the selected authored anchor and the draft respectively.

Also carries the CRAW-28 debt: the owed tail ring on the crawfish (scan IMG_4109 has a tail on its back side) and the whole-body girth hover at 48 to 56 ms per frame on the 920k-face shell, which needs a shallower hover depth, coarser tolerance or a banded triangulation.
definition-of-done: 1. Launch entry 'CRAW-30: Ring Editing (fertility)': F5, R, hover mid-thigh shows the preview; click makes a draft with one cyan authored anchor and white supporting anchors; click the draft on the far side of the limb adds a second authored anchor and the ring passes through it; click an authored anchor to select it (yellow), Delete removes it and the ring re-fits; drag a selected anchor and the ring follows at preview rate; Ctrl+Z restores the anchor; Enter confirms; Esc with no draft leaves the tool keeping the ring. Screenshots of each step under tmp/, driven through the /input routes. 2. The scroll wheel orbits the camera while the tool runs; no tilt binding remains in the HUD or ui-state. 3. Ctrl+S writes the authored anchors only; reloading the .dsl reproduces every confirmed ring element-exact (fingerprint equality), including one whose authored anchors were edited after a first save (replaceSpline in place). 4. An automatic ring_candidates ring becomes a draft on first click and is written as a spline_ring statement. 5. Unit, procedural only: on a tapered tube a draft with two authored anchors passes through both within one edge length; removing one restores the one-anchor ring exactly; the fit never moves or removes an authored anchor over 20 random insertions; a statement written with authored anchors reloads the same edge cycle. 6. Crawfish, repaired via repair_mesh: a tail-segment ring on the back side confirmed and screenshotted; whole-body girth hover measured and either under 16 ms or the remaining cost recorded with the lever tried. 7. ui-state ringTool reports the draft (authored and supporting anchors, selected anchor, undo available) and per confirmed ring its authored anchors. 8. Build checkstyle-green; unit tests load no mesh files.
testing-plan: 1. Procedural unit tests (tube, tapered tube, sphere): authored vs supporting invariants, add/remove/move, reload element-exact. 2. run-scene on fertility driving hover, click, click-far-side, select, Delete, drag, Ctrl+Z, Enter, Esc through the /input routes with a screenshot per step and ui-state checks after each. 3. Same on the repaired crawfish for the tail ring and the girth timing. 4. Reload every saved .dsl and compare fingerprints against the live rings.
unknowns: Whether a moved pin should snap to vertices or allow an inserted vertex at the barycentric hit (CRAW-28 snaps to the nearest vertex)

Whether a dragged authored anchor snaps to the nearest mesh vertex (as insertion does today) or splits the face so it sits exactly under the cursor; start with vertex snap and record the miss distance as pinSnapFraction did
Whether the supporting anchors should be written to the .dsl as well, as a cache, so a reload does not depend on SplineAnchorFit staying deterministic across future changes

ANSWERED (anchor snapping): a click and a drag both snap the authored anchor to the corner of the picked face nearest the hit, as CRAW-28's insertion did; a drag moves only when the cursor reaches a new vertex. Splitting the face is not done.

ANSWERED (supporting anchors in the .dsl): not written. spline_ring re-runs AuthoredSplineRing on evaluate, which is deterministic (fixed summation order, normal round-tripped through the written text before the live trace); reload equality is checked live and in the unit test. A future change to SplineAnchorFit would move saved rings, which is the cost of not caching them.

RULING NEEDED (normal= in the statement): spline_ring now carries normal= next to the authored points, because one or two anchors do not decide a plane on their own and the tool's plane came from the view-independent girdle search at the first click. The alternative is re-deriving it from the limb axis on reload, which needs the skeleton in the node

RULING NEEDED (converted ring_candidates rings): the converted graph ring is hidden only for the session. After a save and reload the ring_candidates ring and its spline_ring conversion both draw (ring_04 and ring_06 on fertility). Suppressing a candidate needs a way to name it in the ring_candidates statement

RULING NEEDED (deleting a confirmed ring): Delete on the last authored anchor of a re-opened ring discards the draft and restores the ring; there is no way to delete a confirmed or saved ring from the tool yet. R with a draft open discards the draft (like Esc) before leaving
Not built: the optional corner anchors (C0 junction) and the explicit tighten-to-neck action the description keeps in scope; neither is in the definition of done or the todos

A drag can leave a sharper corner than a click (fertility: 144.9 deg after the drag vs 152.8 before), since the fit keeps the drag's supporting anchors on the reference plane while the authored one moves off it; the allowance blends the excuse linearly along each segment
changes-made: Authored vs supporting anchors: SurfaceSplineTracer.anchorAuthored (setAnchors(ids, authored, count), insertAnchor(before, vertex, authored)); SplineAnchorFit takes authoredVertexId/authoredPoint/authoredAllowance/authoredCount, places the authored anchors first, fills the widest arc gaps to four, then inserts supporting anchors at the worst deviation; it never moves or removes an authored anchor. The deviation a point may have is excused by its segment's authored ends' own distance off the reference loop, blended linearly, so the spline can bend through an off-plane click without the fit crowding supporting anchors round it.

New paths.AuthoredSplineRing: the ring an authored anchor set decides, a pure function of (anchor set, which leads, base normal). Plane: one anchor takes the base normal; two take the plane through both nearest the base normal; three or more take the least-squares plane plus BASE_NORMAL_PULL 0.25 of the scatter's trace pulling toward the base normal (a plane exactly through three clicks, two of them close, ran lengthwise down the fertility thigh: 143 edges, length 301; with the pull 49 edges, 150.3 deg). The plane is cut through the first anchor's vertex, supporting anchors are fitted at depth 2 (FIT_DEPTH) and the ring re-traced at depth 3. Summation is in vertex-id order so reordering anchors never changes a bit.

spline_ring gains normal= (the base normal); points= holds the authored anchors only and the node re-runs AuthoredSplineRing on evaluate. RingDslWriter.appendSpline/replaceSpline/splineStatement take the base normal (replaceSpline adds normal= to a line that lacks one). The tool traces live rings from the normal after one round trip through the %.6f text format, so reload is element-exact by construction.

RingTool rewritten around a draft: R starts; hover previews the one-anchor ring through the face corner under the cursor (exactly what a click drafts); click drafts it (cyan authored anchor, white supporting); with a draft, click an authored anchor selects it (yellow), click elsewhere adds an authored anchor, press on an authored anchor and drag moves it with a depth-2 re-trace per frame and a depth-3 re-trace on release, Delete/Backspace removes the selected anchor (the last one discards the draft), Ctrl+Z undoes the last anchor edit once, Enter confirms, Esc discards the draft, Esc with no draft leaves the tool keeping every ring. A click on a confirmed ring re-opens it as the draft (Enter puts it back in place, unsaved only if its anchors changed; Esc restores it); a click on a ring_candidates ring converts it (anchors fitted to its edge loop, all authored, base normal = their plane) and hides the graph ring for the session. Clicks are queued and run on the next frame against a fresh pick, so an automation click no longer acts on the previous hover.

Scroll tilt removed: OrbitMouseTrap.toolScroll gone, the wheel zooms the orbit camera with the tool running (fertility: distance 268.5 -> 186.3 on three ticks, tool active); RingTool tilt fields and ui-state tiltAboutView/tiltAboutTangent gone; GirdlingPlane keeps its tilt fields for other producers. OrbitMouseTrap gains toolGrab/toolRelease so a press on an authored anchor drags it instead of orbiting. MeshViewerKeyGuy leaves Ctrl+Z to the scene (plain Z still toggles wireframe). Keys.DELETE (261) added. New /input/drag route (ixdar-cli drag --fromX --fromY --toX --toY --steps) draws a frame after every step.

Drawing: MeshOverlayRuntime.setHandleMarkers draws the authored anchors as larger per-colour spheres (cyan 0x00E5FF, selected 0xFFE000) over the white supporting markers; ring colour 0x00E5D0 and 0xFF6B6B replaced so no ring shares the anchor cyan or the preview pink. ui-state ringTool: draft block (exists, authoredAnchors, supportingAnchors, counts, selectedAnchor, hoveredAnchor, dragging, undoAvailable, reopenedRing, convertedFrom, baseNormal, edgeCount, length, millis, fingerprint), per confirmed ring authoredAnchorCount/authoredAnchors/baseNormal, hoveredGraphRing, lastRow.

Girth hover lever (exact, result-identical): SplineAnchorFit measured every traced point against every reference span (the 1223-crossing whole-body girth made scanDeviation half the fit, 64 of 121 profile samples). It now bounds each run of 32 reference spans with a box and skips a run whose box is farther than the best span so far, starting from the run the last query ended in; SurfaceSpline.spanDistanceSquared is the shared per-span measure, so the distance is equal to the bit (fertility draft fingerprints 64917fd2ba3a8628 / 4999f93def8d5a53 / 39f1d86b188b4062 unchanged before and after).

MEASURED, DoD 6 timing NOT under 16 ms: crawfish (repaired, 938302 faces), view from below, preview frame including GPU pick, plane search and fit. Whole-body girth (1223-1230 crossings, 6-7 anchors, 264-352 geodesics): 46-56 ms before, 25-31 ms after the culling (warm). Tail and abdomen points (517-675 crossings, 9-12 anchors, 528-715 geodesics): 21-33 ms before, 18-23 ms after. Lever tried and rejected: fitting the hover one bisection shallower (depth 1) cut the girth's geodesics from 264 to 128 but raised the frame to 73-76 ms, because each leaf geodesic doubles in length and A*/FlipOut cost grows faster than length on a fine mesh. What remains (async-profiler, tmp/craw30_girth_profile2.html): geodesics are ~70 percent of previewAt (SurfaceGeodesics.seedWalk A* and FlipGeodesics.shorten about equal), the plane search 17 percent, the deviation scan now 9 percent. The next lever is fewer geodesics per fit (the fit re-traces four segments per inserted anchor) or a cheaper seed than a fresh A* per midpoint.

Crawfish tail (DoD 6): scan IMG_4109's tail is curled under the carapace on its back side; from below (orbit azimuth 1.5708, elevation -1.2) a hover at (520,880) previews a 9-anchor ring round the tail fan's base, and the click drafts and Enter confirms it: 1 authored + 8 supporting anchors, 335 edges, length 0.53067, sharpest corner 131.4 deg (below 150, within the scan-limit ruling CRAW-28 recorded), fingerprint cb0c3c4536c6fd1e. Screenshots tmp/craw30_crawfish_tail_hover.png, tmp/craw30_crawfish_tail_draft_side.png, tmp/craw30_crawfish_tail_ring_confirmed.png.

Fertility, launch entry 'CRAW-30: Ring Editing (fertility)' (ixdar.mesh.dsl=fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl), driven by tmp/craw30_sequence.sh through /input: R, hover (660,560) mid-thigh previews a 4-anchor ring over a 79-crossing girdle; click drafts 1 authored + 3 supporting, 38 edges, fingerprint 64917fd2ba3a8628; orbit to the far side, click (262,455) adds a second authored anchor and the ring passes through it: 2 + 2, 50 edges, 4999f93def8d5a53; click the anchor selects it (yellow); Delete re-fits to exactly the one-anchor ring (64917fd2ba3a8628 again); Ctrl+Z restores it (4999f93def8d5a53); drag (260,461)->(300,425) in 8 steps moves it, re-tracing at depth 2 per frame and depth 3 in 1 to 6 ms on release (39f1d86b188b4062); Ctrl+Z restores the pre-drag ring; Enter confirms ring 5 (unsaved); Esc leaves the tool keeping it. Screenshots tmp/craw30_00_start.png .. tmp/craw30_10_tool_left_ring_kept.png.

Save and reload (DoD 3, 4), tmp/craw30_save.sh on a copy of the fixture in tmp/ so the tracked fixture is never written: the wheel zooms while the tool runs (distance 268.5 -> 186.3); ring A (2 authored) and ring_04 of ring_candidates, converted on click to 5 authored anchors (d461ec025836a33d), confirmed and Ctrl+S appended ring_05 and ring_06 as spline_ring statements with points= the authored anchors and normal=; ring A re-opened by clicking it, a third authored anchor added (3 + 4, 49 edges, c0a387a483e9b63d), Enter and Ctrl+S rewrote ring_05 in place (0 appended, 1 rewritten). Relaunching on the saved file reloads ring_05 as 49 edges c0a387a483e9b63d and ring_06 as 33 edges d461ec025836a33d, both equal to the live rings. Screenshots tmp/craw30_11_graph_ring_converted_to_draft.png .. tmp/craw30_14_reloaded.png.

Unit (procedural, no mesh files), unit.mesh.SurfaceSplineTest 9/9: aDraftWithTwoAuthoredAnchorsPassesThroughBoth (tapered tube, both authored anchors within one mean edge of the ring, no corner under 150 deg), removingAnAuthoredAnchorRestoresTheOneAnchorRingExactly (anchors, polyline and edge marks array-equal), theFitNeverMovesOrRemovesAnAuthoredAnchor (20 seeded random insertions, every authored vertex held and flagged, the first still leading), theWrittenStatementReloadsTheSameRing (two authored anchors plus normal through spline_ring reload the same edge cycle, with supporting anchors re-fitted). Full unit suite: Tests run: 321, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0.
